claim: A dossier change whose target the user has locked has no defined outcome. §7.7's precedence (lock > dossier existence > assignment > …) and §7.1's first outcome row (an edit targeting a locked entity or path is refused; 'a host that must override a lock sends an unlock first') meet §7.7 items 2, 11 and 14 (the dossier is the sole immutable truth; a listed ruin is present as its ruin; dossier-owned values change only by dossier events) when a dossier removal, a `ruined` state, a rename, a kind or class change, a re-designation or a `knownTo` / concealment change targets a dossier-backed element, or its building, that the user locked; likewise in an epoch, DR28's calamity F5 targets are 'struck in place, never relocated' while §4.11's hazard exemptions say 'a locked or pinned entity is never struck'. The port sends no unlock (V08 has no such rule), the change is no map event the outcome table can answer with actions, and refusing it leaves the map contradicting the dossier, which §5.3's stage-end coherence row (a hard invariant) aborts — a lost dossier change — while applying it silently breaks the user's lock. Two rules, two outcomes, no rung, no test.
required_change: In §7.7, directly after the precedence paragraph, add the one statement: '**A dossier change meets a lock or a pin on its own target** (items 20, 22). A lock or a pin binds map events, placements and an epoch's own steps, never a dossier fact: a dossier change — standalone or carried by an epoch (§7.7 item 6), a calamity's F5 targets (DR28) among them — whose target is a dossier-backed element, its building or a dossier-owned path of it (§7.7 item 11) that the user locked or pinned is applied as its least-disruption mutation (§7.7 item 5), changing only what the fact requires (a removal closes the use and leaves the building standing vacant; a `ruined` state ruins the building in place; a rename, kind, class or knowledge change sets the value). Each lock and pin it overrides is kept on whatever the change leaves standing, orphaned (§7.4's orphan table) where its target goes, and listed in the event's `DisruptionReport.why` with the rule `lockOverridden`, never silently; §4.11's exemption that a locked or pinned entity is never struck holds for the engine's own hazards only. The precedence line stands for placement: a dossier element is never placed on a locked entity.' Add `lockOverridden` to the rule words V09 §4.9 renders for `DisruptionReport.why`. Add to §13.2's *Derivation fills every gap* list: '(T20-14) on B-DOSSIER-lite, a dossier removal, a `ruined` state, a calamity F5 strike in an epoch, a rename and a re-designation of a locked element, and of a pinned one, are each applied, the lock or pin listed `lockOverridden` and kept or orphaned as stated, and the coherence rows pass (§5.3)'.

claim: Two stream-key components have no bound and no outcome at their cap (§6.1). The epoch component is packed as u16 with its upper half reserved to the history replay (`0x8000 + r`, 'so no replay draw can equal a live epoch's'), but a document's live epoch index has no stated bound: each `advance` adds up to `advance.maxEpochs` (200) epochs and nothing caps a document's total, so past 0x7FFF a live epoch's keys equal a replay epoch's and past 0xFFFF the component wraps onto epoch 0's draws. The salt is packed as u16 and bumped by every town-wide `rerollLayer`, with no bound either. The reroll component has its cap (32 767, `no_alternative`); these two do not, and §6.1's distinctness test cannot reach the case — a silent stream collision.
required_change: In §6.1's components list: (epoch) 'pack the epoch component as u32 — the packed components take one more 32-bit lane in the stream key's finaliser round —, key the history replay's coarse epochs `0x8000_0000 + r`, and bound a document's live epoch index at 0x7FFF_FFFF: an `epoch` event past it is an empty edit with the reason `epochCap` (§7.1 *Empty edits*), and an `advance` that would pass it bends to the epochs that fit, said in one line'; (salt) 'a town-wide salt is bounded at 0xFFFF: a `rerollLayer` whose concern's salt stands at the bound reports `no_alternative` and appends nothing (§7.1 *Empty edits*)'. Update J-A113.61's row to the new replay base. Add to §6.1's *Distinctness* test: 'and on a fixture whose live epoch index stands at the bound and whose `naming` salt stands at 0xFFFF, the next epoch and the next `rerollLayer(naming)` take the stated outcomes, and no live epoch's key equals a replay epoch's'.

claim: Nothing defines one town open in two tabs or windows of the standalone app. Every town lives in one IndexedDB database per origin (V09 §2.11: `docs`, `journal`, `drafts`), every commit is journalled there against the tab's own `logHead`, compaction replaces `LocalDocRecord.snapshot` (V09 §3.8), and an unshared document has one stored session whose undo is linear (§7.4). Two tabs editing one town each fold their own log, interleave journal entries and overwrite each other's snapshot; at the next open recovery meets the first `logHeadAfter` mismatch and quarantines the 'later changes' (§3.8 (3)) — committed edits lost from the town — with no rule, rung or test.
required_change: Add V09 §3.8 item 7, '**One tab writes a town.** Opening a town for editing takes the Web Locks API lock `plat-doc:<docId>` (`navigator.locks.request`, mode `exclusive`, held for the tab's life); a second tab or window that opens the town while the lock is held opens it read-only — it writes no journal entry and runs no compaction, every tool is disabled, and the banner `info.openElsewhere` ("This town is open in another tab.") carries `button.editHere`, which asks the holder over `BroadcastChannel('plat-doc')` to finish its pending journal write, compact and release; the asking tab then takes the lock and re-opens from the new snapshot. A browser without Web Locks uses a lease in `LocalDocRecord` (`leaseTab`, `leaseUntil`, renewed every 5 s and expired after 15 s) with the same outcome; a holder killed mid-write releases its lock with the tab, and recovery runs as item 3 states. In host mode the host is the store (§11.3) and no lock is taken.' Add `leaseTab` and `leaseUntil` to V09 §2.11's `LocalDocRecord` with their lifecycle row, the two keys to V09 §4.9's catalogue, a row to V09 §3.16 (e) ('autosave and recovery: the same town opened in a second tab → read-only with **Edit here**; rung check'), and to T-V9-17: 'two tabs on one town: the second opens read-only and writes nothing; after **Edit here** every edit the first tab committed is in the snapshot the second opens (0 lost edits); a killed holder's lock passes to the waiting tab'.

claim: Two cases of an `advance` job have no outcome (V06 §4.1, §6). (1) A job that ends without Stop — the tab closed, the app or the worker killed: the epochs already folded survive through V09 §3.8's journal, but the group's last epoch carries neither `stoppedAt` nor `index + 1 = of`, and nothing says whether the next open resumes the job, reads the group as stopped, or tells the user. (2) An edit, a clerk acceptance or an undo on the same document while the job folds epochs: V06 §6 says the job never blocks 'an edit on another document', so an edit on this one would land between the group's epochs, breaking the group's contiguity and its one-step undo ('while its last epoch is the latest live event'), and no rule says whether the tools wait or the job stops first.
required_change: Add to V06 §4.1, after *Undo*: '**A job cut off.** An `advance` job that ends without Stop leaves the epochs already folded as a shorter group, as Stop does: at the next open the app writes nothing, reads a group whose last epoch has `index + 1 < of` and no `stoppedAt` as stopped at `index + 1`, never resumes the job by itself, and the history panel shows "Advanced {n} of {m} years — stopped" with **Continue**, which starts a new `advance` for the remaining span from the document's week. **Edits during a job.** While a job folds epochs on a document, every tool, the clerk's Accept and undo on that document wait — the rail and the drawer show the job's progress, as V09 §3.9's going back does — until Stop or the job's end; edits on other documents never wait.' Add T-V6-23 clause (j): 'a 100-epoch job killed after epoch 37: the reopened document holds 37 epochs read as stopped at 37, no job resumes, **Continue** appends a new group for the remaining span; during a job the tools and Accept on that document are disabled and a queued undo waits for the job's end'. Add the two cases to V06 §3.21's `advance` rows.

claim: A numeric table column may declare no range, so its cells have no ends: `ColumnSpec.range` is optional (V11 §2.1), and V11 §4.1's clamp and rule (a)'s compile check act only on a declared range. A numeric cell of a column with none — V06 §2.2's `advance.maxEpochs`, `replay.maxEpochs`, `history.checkpointStride`, `uses.openCandidates` among them — takes 0, a negative or an arbitrarily large value from `editTable`, a pack, an override or a calibration run with no outcome stated; for a divisor (`⌈spanYears × 52 ÷ advance.maxEpochs⌉` in V06 §3.3.2; the keyframe period) the rule then has no finite value.
required_change: In V11 §2.1, make `ColumnSpec.range` required for `type: 'number'` and `'integer'` (a count or divisor column's lower bound at least 1); V11 §3.2.1 step 4 refuses a numeric column without one, naming it; T-V11-3 gains 'every number and integer column of every registry table declares its range, and every count or divisor column's lower bound is at least 1'; V11 §3.26 rule (a) adds 'an edit, a pack, an override or a calibration run is clamped into its column's declared range (V11 §4.1; V12 §3.7), so no runtime reader meets a value outside it'.
